patterns.fix: Replace each verdict with the fact behind it: a number, a date, a named customer, a shipped thing. Tell the AI: 'Do not use testament, pivotal, crucial role or evolving landscape. State facts only.'

patterns.name: The Any-Company Paragraph
patterns.oneLiner: Body copy so generic that swapping in a competitor's name changes nothing.
patterns.fix: Run the substitution test: replace your name with a competitor's. If the paragraph survives, add one fact only you can state: a client, a figure, a process step, a date. Feed those facts to the AI instead of asking it to invent them.

patterns.name: The Ensuring Tail
patterns.oneLiner: Feature sentences end with a tacked-on '-ing' clause that claims a benefit: ', ensuring seamless collaboration.'
patterns.fix: Cut the trailing clause. If a real consequence was hiding in it, give it its own sentence with a number or a condition: 'Data syncs every five minutes. Edits made offline merge when you reconnect.'

patterns.name: The Invented Framework

patterns.oneLiner: Every sentence in a block is roughly the same length, so the copy has an even, mechanical rhythm.

patterns.name: The Baked-In Checkerboard
patterns.oneLiner: A 'transparent' PNG from an image model has the grey-and-white checkerboard painted into the pixels.
patterns.fix: Use a model or API option that outputs true RGBA, or run a background-removal step, then check the file's alpha channel before shipping.

patterns.name: The Default Person
patterns.oneLiner: Generated people follow stereotypes: CEOs and judges are light-skinned men, low-paid workers are darker-skinned women.

patterns.name: The Dish Nobody Cooked

patterns.name: The Ethereal Default

patterns.fix: Write a style brief before generating: palette, lighting, lens, texture and references you own. Generate against that brief, and reject outputs that look like the tool's default.

patterns.name: The False AI Label

patterns.name: The Glowing Brain

patterns.name: The Sparkle in the Corner

patterns.oneLiner: Cold emails lead with what 'we' do and 'our' platform before saying anything about the reader.
patterns.fix: Give the tool one concrete fact about the recipient's situation and tell it to open with that. Limit 'we' and 'our' to one sentence.

patterns.oneLiner: Every AI-generated slide is titled with a topic like 'Market Overview' instead of the point it makes.
patterns.fix: Ask the tool to write each title as a full-sentence claim, such as 'Revenue grew 12% after the price change', and to make the slide body the evidence for it.

patterns.name: Twenty Slides Saying Little
patterns.oneLiner: A topic that needs five slides becomes twenty, each with one thin idea.
patterns.fix: Set the slide count yourself, ask the tool to merge slides that share a point, and delete agenda and divider slides in short decks.

Your AI Presentations Look Great but Say Nothing

patterns.name: Best Of, Never Touched
patterns.oneLiner: A 'best products' review list with affiliate links and no sign anyone used the products.
patterns.fix: Only publish reviews with your own photos, measurements and reasons for each ranking. Tell the AI tool to draft from your test notes, never from spec sheets.

How To Write Reviews

patterns.name: Books Under Your Name
patterns.oneLiner: Generated books are listed for sale credited to a real, known author who never wrote them.
patterns.fix: Platforms should verify author identity before a name is linked to an existing author profile and act on impersonation reports without demanding a trademark. Authors can monitor their profiles for new titles.

patterns.name: Docs For An API That Isn't
patterns.oneLiner: Generated documentation or examples call methods, flags and arguments the library never had.
patterns.fix: Run every code sample in CI against the real library version. Ground the AI tool in the actual API reference and reject calls it cannot find there.

sources.t: On Mitigating Code LLM Hallucinations with API Documentation

patterns.name: Hidden Text For The Bot
patterns.oneLiner: Pages hide text that only AI search and assistants read, to steer what they say about a product.
patterns.fix: AI search should ignore hidden content and treat page text as data, not instructions. Site owners should never hide text; Google already treats hidden text as spam.

Spam Policies for Google Web Search

patterns.name: Not Widely Documented
patterns.oneLiner: Text fills a gap by announcing the information is scarce, then guesses what it likely is.
patterns.fix: If the information is missing, leave the section out. Tell the AI tool: 'If you cannot find a source, say nothing on that point.'

sources.t: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

patterns.name: Notability By Assertion
patterns.oneLiner: A page proves its subject matters by listing kinds of coverage, like 'featured in national media outlets'.
patterns.fix: State what the subject did and cite the coverage directly, or leave it out. Tell the AI tool not to describe types of media coverage or social media presence.

The Rise of AI-Generated Content in Wikipedia

patterns.name: The Composer Post
patterns.oneLiner: Long professional posts written by the platform's built-in AI composer, all in the same polished voice.
patterns.fix: Write posts from a specific thing you did or saw, and use AI only to tighten them. Platforms should label AI-composed posts and comments.

sources.t: How LinkedIn opened the door to AI slop

patterns.name: The Engagement Bait Image
patterns.oneLiner: Feeds fill with uncanny AI images posted in volume to farm reactions and send people to ad sites.
patterns.fix: Platforms should label generated images and demote high-volume pages that post them with copy-paste captions. Users can check whether a page's history is all generated content.

patterns.name: The Evolving Landscape Opener
patterns.oneLiner: An article opens with a paragraph about how fast the field is changing before saying anything specific.
patterns.fix: Delete the opening paragraph and start with the answer or the first step. Tell the AI tool: 'No preamble, no scene-setting, first sentence must contain a fact.'

AI Tells | Graphite

patterns.name: The Generated Sales Rep
patterns.oneLiner: Sales outreach profiles use a generated face and a made-up person to start conversations.
patterns.fix: Use real staff with real photos for outreach, or a clearly labelled automated account. Platforms can detect generated faces and require identity checks for outreach accounts.

patterns.name: The Invented Byline
patterns.oneLiner: Articles credited to a writer who does not exist, with a generated headshot and a homely bio.
patterns.fix: Credit real people who actually reviewed the piece, and disclose automation where readers would ask how it was made. If no human wrote or checked it, do not invent one.

patterns.oneLiner: Generated docs or tutorials tell you to install a package that does not exist, or that an attacker registered.
patterns.fix: Check every package name against the official registry and its real maintainer before publishing an install line. Pin versions and use lockfiles.

patterns.oneLiner: A security report written by a chatbot describes a 'novel exploit' in functions that do not exist.
patterns.fix: Do not submit any report a human has not verified against the actual code. Projects can require AI disclosure, rate-limit new reporters and ban repeat slop submitters.

patterns.oneLiner: A README with a badge row, emoji headings, a Features table and boilerplate Contributing steps, but no real usage.
patterns.fix: Lead with one sentence on what the project does, then a working install and usage example. Keep only badges that carry real status, and delete template sections with nothing project-specific in them.

patterns.name: The Untested Field Guide
patterns.oneLiner: A generated guide to a dangerous activity is sold as expert advice, with no AI disclosure.
patterns.fix: Platforms should require AI disclosure and expert review for safety-critical guides and remove unverified ones on report. Buyers should check that the author is traceable and the publisher is known.

patterns.name: Tortured Phrases
patterns.oneLiner: Standard terms are swapped for odd synonyms, like 'counterfeit consciousness' for artificial intelligence.
patterns.fix: Never run technical writing through spinning or paraphrase tools. Reviewers can screen manuscripts against known tortured-phrase lists.

patterns.oneLiner: Ads sell AI-powered or pre-built online stores with promised passive income.

patterns.name: Billed For Unasked Work
patterns.oneLiner: An AI builder does work nobody requested, like redesigning the whole app, and charges for it.
patterns.fix: Show a plan and a cost estimate before large changes, keep edits to the files the request names, and do not charge for reverted work the user did not ask for.

patterns.name: Cheaper On The Price List
patterns.oneLiner: The model with the lower per-token price costs more in practice because it uses far more tokens.

patterns.name: Coupons Without Rules
patterns.oneLiner: AI-generated discount code logic checks that a code exists but ignores expiry, usage limits and stacking.
patterns.fix: Validate coupons on the server with expiry, per-customer and total usage limits, and an explicit stacking rule, and never ship the code list to the client.

patterns.name: Forgeable Payment Webhook
patterns.oneLiner: The AI-built payment webhook trusts any request, so a forged 'payment succeeded' event unlocks paid features.
patterns.fix: Tell the AI: verify every webhook with the provider's signature check on the raw body, reject invalid ones, and fetch the event from the provider before acting.

patterns.fix: Ship with a hard spend cap at the plan price, require an explicit opt-in to overage, and warn in the product at 50, 80 and 100 percent of included usage.

patterns.oneLiner: The same message costs several times more in tokens when written in a non-English language.

patterns.oneLiner: Users pay for hidden reasoning and output tokens they cannot see or verify.

patterns.oneLiner: Early in the chat the model commits to an assumption and keeps building on it after you correct it.

patterns.oneLiner: You ask the agent to run or explain something, and it starts editing files instead.
patterns.fix: Classify requests as read-only or write before acting and keep read-only requests in a no-edit mode. Ask before making changes when the user asked a question.

patterns.oneLiner: When your exact choice is unavailable, the agent quietly picks a near alternative and carries on.
patterns.fix: Treat stated values as hard constraints by default and stop to ask when one cannot be met. If substitution is allowed, show the change prominently before committing.

patterns.name: Cut Off Mid-Thought
patterns.oneLiner: A voice assistant decides you have finished speaking during a short pause and starts answering.
patterns.fix: Use semantic end-of-turn detection or a longer silence window, and set eagerness low for open questions. Let users hold a key or say 'wait' to keep the turn.

patterns.oneLiner: AI search turns a satirical post or a forum joke into a confident instruction.
patterns.fix: Down-rank satire and joke-heavy user content for advice queries, and refuse to summarise when the only matching sources are forums. Show the source type, such as 'forum reply', beside the claim.

patterns.name: Guess Instead of Ask
patterns.oneLiner: Given an ambiguous detail that changes the outcome, the agent picks one reading and acts on it.
patterns.fix: When alternatives lead to different actions, ask one short question before acting. When you do assume, state the assumption in the result so it can be corrected.

patterns.fix: Warn before an edit forks a long thread, show branches as a visible tree or list, and let users name, compare and return to any branch. Never remove access to an old path.

patterns.fix: Detect future-tense promises in replies when no background task exists and replace them with the work or an honest limit. If background jobs exist, show them as real tasks with status in the interface.

patterns.oneLiner: The rules you set at the start of the chat stop being followed a few turns later.

patterns.oneLiner: A browsing assistant obeys commands hidden in the web page it was only asked to read.
patterns.fix: Treat all page and file content as untrusted data, check every proposed action against the user's original request, and require explicit confirmation for sending, logging in or reading other sites. Keep agent browsing separate from the user's normal logged-in profile.

patterns.oneLiner: You write in Spanish or Sinhala and the assistant answers, or slides mid-reply, into English.
patterns.fix: Detect the user's language and pin the reply language in the system prompt. Run a language check on the output and regenerate any reply that switches language without being asked.

patterns.name: Memory That Follows You
patterns.oneLiner: Details from old chats quietly shape new answers in unrelated tasks, and you cannot see why.
patterns.fix: Show a small 'used memory' marker with the facts it used, let users edit or delete each item, and scope memory to a project or space. Offer a one-click temporary chat with memory off.

patterns.oneLiner: The agent finishes a task but leaves no readable record of what it opened, changed or sent.
patterns.fix: Keep a step-by-step activity log for every agent run, with each action, target and result, and link it from the completion message. Let users export it and set how long it is kept.

patterns.oneLiner: Starter prompts under the input box suggest tasks the assistant cannot actually do.

patterns.name: The Answer Avalanche
patterns.oneLiner: A simple question gets a wall of text, background, caveats and extras instead of the answer.

patterns.name: The Clippy Interrupt
patterns.oneLiner: A copilot pushes suggestions while you are mid-task, pulling attention away from what you were doing.

patterns.name: The Doom Loop to Nowhere

patterns.fix: Show a visible human handoff from the first turn and trigger it automatically after two unresolved turns or any mention of a dispute. Pass the transcript to the person so the customer does not repeat themselves.

patterns.name: The Pretend Read
patterns.oneLiner: Given a link or file it could not open, the assistant writes a confident summary anyway.

patterns.oneLiner: The agent repeats the same failing step again and again instead of changing approach or stopping.

patterns.oneLiner: The bot cannot do what you asked but spends a paragraph of workarounds before saying so.

patterns.oneLiner: The assistant says it could not find something without saying where it looked.

Guidelines for human-AI interaction design

patterns.name: The Victory Lap
patterns.oneLiner: The agent's completion report is a checklist of green ticks and 'production-ready' claims nobody verified.
patterns.fix: Require each claim in a completion report to link to evidence such as a command output or test log, and ban hype terms like 'production-ready' in agent instructions. Report what was not checked.

patterns.name: Twenty Questions Intake
patterns.oneLiner: The assistant asks a list of clarifying questions before doing anything, even when a good default exists.
patterns.fix: Ask at most one question, and only when different answers lead to different actions. Otherwise state the assumption, deliver, and invite correction.

patterns.name: The Photo From The Item Name
patterns.oneLiner: Delivery app menus show a generated dish photo drawn from the item's name, not the restaurant's real food.
patterns.fix: Use only photos of the real dish, or show no photo. If a platform generates one, have the restaurant approve it first and label it as an illustration on the listing.

patterns.name: Facts Nobody Gave
patterns.oneLiner: AI site builders fill a small business site with prices, hours, policies and perks the owner never supplied.
patterns.fix: Tell the tool: use only facts from my brief, and leave a marked gap for anything missing. Before launch, check every price, time, policy, guarantee and contact detail against the brief and delete what you cannot confirm.

patterns.name: The Fake Send
patterns.oneLiner: A generated contact form says your message was sent, but nothing is sent or stored anywhere.
patterns.fix: Show success only after a real endpoint confirms the message was received. Until the form is wired, say plainly on the page that nothing was sent, and send a test message to your own inbox before launch.
